title: SPCX Q3-results lock-up release — ~1.3 billion shares (28% of the 180-day cohort) two trading days after Oct 20 results
source: EST: date derived, not read as a date. SEC: 424B4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026042639/spaceexplorationtechnologi.htm, fetched 2026-10-20, HTTP 200, read in full) releases 'up to 1.3 billion shares of Class A common stock, representing 28% of the shares subject to the 180-day lock-up period' on 'the second full trading day on Nasdaq immediately following the public release of our quarterly financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026' (the lock-up agreement text adds that 'flash' numbers or preliminary, partial earnings do not count). NEWS: SpaceX's own announcement, filed on its IR site 2026-10-16 as 'SpaceX to Post Third Quarter 2026 Results and Host Webcast on October 20, 2026' (title and wire coverage read; the ir.spacex.com page itself returned 403 and the q4cdn PDF text is font-encoded, so the body was not machine-read), puts the release after the close on 2026-10-20, so the first full trading day is Wed 10-21 and the second is Thu 2026-10-22. Precedent: the Q2 8-K was filed 2026-08-04 16:01 ET (EDGAR) and the first earnings stage opened 08-06. Estimate because the Q3 release had not happened when this was researched (2026-10-20 ~11:30 ET); it flips to confirmed once the results are public (a slip to 10-21 after the close moves the date to 10-23)
notes: Largest single stage left in the 180-day cohort: up to ~1.3B Class A shares, ~17.6% of 7,380M Class A outstanding, ~2.3x the 555.6M-share IPO float and ~16 days of 20-day average volume (81.7M). Relative to the tradable pool it is smaller than the first earnings stage was (+46% of ~2.82B eligible-plus-float vs +164% of the IPO float on 2026-08-06). Insider sales are capped by Rule 144 volume limits and by affiliates' exclusion from some stages, so 'eligible' is an upper bound; the Aug 6 stage saw 255.2M traded against 911.5M eligible (28%). The Q3 print itself lands first (reaction session 10-21) and will dominate the tape; read docs/research/events/spcx-lockup-release-2026-10-22.md before reading this as a pure supply event. Superseded the proposal spcx-lockup-release-2026-10-22.from-spcx-lockup-expiry-2026-12-08.json.
